html:
Oudh, or Awadh, was a state on the middle Ganges plain of north India, between Delhi and Bengal, from 1722 to 1856. It began as a Mughal province. Its governor Saadat Khan and his heirs, the Nawabs of Awadh, ruled it as their own as the Mughal Empire weakened.

In 1764 Nawab Shuja ud Daula lost the battle of Buxar to the East India Company. After that Oudh paid for Company troops and slowly lost its freedom. In 1775 the capital moved to Lucknow, which grew into a centre of Urdu poetry, Shia Muslim ritual, music and cooking. In 1801 the Company forced it to give up about half its land. In 1819 the nawab took the title of king.

In 1856 the Company annexed Oudh and sent its last king, Wajid Ali Shah, into exile. Many sepoys came from Oudh, and the annexation helped spark the Indian Rebellion the next year.
